final_answer: In special relativity, the speed of light (c) is the ultimate speed limit because of the way space and time are interwoven. As an object with mass accelerates, its relativistic mass increases according to the Lorentz factor, γ = 1/√(1 - v²/c²). As velocity (v) approaches c, γ approaches infinity, meaning infinite energy would be required to accelerate the object further. This makes exceeding c physically impossible. Additionally, time dilation and length contraction effects become extreme near c, ensuring that no frame of reference can surpass this speed. The invariance of the speed of light in all inertial frames is a foundational postulate of special relativity, making c an absolute cosmic speed limit.
